notes.meaning: The priest pours the rest of the olive oil in his hand onto the head of the person being cleansed. This completed the atonement—making peace between God and the person—just as was done for a wealthier worshiper. It showed the healed person that God welcomed them back fully, treating them with dignity and care.

The priest sacrifices the two birds the poor person brought, offering one as a sin offering to deal with wrongdoing and the other as a burnt offering of wholehearted dedication to the Lord. Along with the grain gift, this completed the full cleansing before God. The Lord made sure that having less money never kept anyone from being restored to worship.

This rule concludes the special instructions for someone who had a skin disease but could not afford the costly three lambs. God provided an affordable path so that every person received the exact same cleansing and honor. His grace was open to everyone, no matter their wealth.

The Lord delivers new instructions to Moses and Aaron together. Aaron was included because inspecting houses and judging purity was the sacred duty of the priests. God spoke directly to their leaders so the whole nation would know how to handle these situations.

God looks ahead to the time when Israel would settle into permanent stone houses in Canaan instead of wandering in tents. He speaks of mildew or mold appearing on a house as something under His sovereign control in the land He gave them. This reminded the people that their homes, just like their bodies, belonged to the Lord and were to be kept pure.

A homeowner who spots strange rot or mold on the walls must immediately go and tell the priest. The owner was instructed to say it looked like mildew rather than declaring the problem himself. Only God's appointed priest had the authority to judge whether a home was ritually clean or unclean.

Before the priest enters to examine the wall, he orders the family to empty out all their furniture and belongings. This protected the household goods, because things did not become ritually unclean until the priest made an official ruling. God showed practical mercy by preventing the family from losing all their possessions.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: An older Catholic commentary says the things taken out could be used freely afterward, unless signs of the problem later showed up on clothing.

notes.meaning: The priest inspects the wall to see if the marks are greenish or reddish and sunk deeper than the plaster surface. Depressions that went deeper than the surface showed that the rot had invaded the stones themselves. Just like deep skin sores on a person, this meant the problem was serious and needed careful attention.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: The Hebrew word for 'depressions' is uncertain. Some translate it 'streaks' or 'eruptions.' 'Wall' here means the plaster surface.

notes.meaning: After seeing the suspicious marks, the priest steps outside and shuts the house up for seven days. Quarantining the building kept people out and gave time to see whether the blight was alive and spreading. Taking time ensured that no hasty or unfair decision was made.

On the seventh day, the priest returns to reinspect the quarantined house. He looks closely to see if the discoloration or cavities have spread across the wall. Spreading was the sure sign that the contamination was an active, harmful decay.

The priest orders the damaged stones to be pulled out and the inside plaster scraped off all the surrounding walls. Both the tainted stones and the scraped dust had to be dumped in an unclean place outside the city. This drastic step removed the rot to keep the rest of the building and the community safe.

Fresh, sound stones were set in place of the infected ones, and the house was covered with a new layer of plaster. The owner was given every opportunity to repair the home and make it sound again. God provided a path for healing and restoration before calling for total destruction.

If the mildew reappears after the old stones were removed and the house was replastered, the priest returns for another inspection. If the mold has spread again, it is diagnosed as a destructive, incurable rot. The priest must then declare the entire house unclean.

The condemned building had to be torn down completely, including its stones, wooden beams, and plaster. All the debris was carted outside the city to an unclean place where garbage lay. Incurable corruption could not remain in the middle of God's holy camp.

Anyone who simply stepped inside the quarantined house became ceremonially unclean until sundown. If someone spent longer there by eating a meal or sleeping, they had to wash their clothes as well. This reminded God's people that lingering around corrupt things brings defilement that must be washed away.

If the priest finds that the mold has not returned or spread after the house was replastered, he pronounces the home clean. The repairs had succeeded, and the destructive contamination was gone. The family was then free to live in their home in peace and safety.

To purify the restored house, the priest takes two live, clean birds, along with cedar wood, red yarn, and a hyssop branch. He slaughters one bird over fresh water in a clay pot. This prepared the blood and living water needed for the ritual cleansing.

The priest dips the living bird, cedar wood, red yarn, and hyssop into the bird's blood and fresh water, and sprinkles the house seven times. He purifies the walls using all these prescribed items. This ceremony visibly cleansed the building from the stain and shadow of decay.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some popular teachers read each item in this kind of rite as a picture of the cross. The cedar is the cross, the scarlet is Jesus' robe, the hyssop is the sponge of vinegar, and the blood and water are from his pierced side.

notes.meaning: The priest releases the living bird into the open fields outside the city, making atonement for the house so it becomes fully clean. Letting the bird fly away showed that the contamination had been carried far away, never to return. God thus reclaimed the dwelling so His people could live there safely.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The Catholic Douay-Rheims Bible says the priest 'shall pray for the house' where other versions say 'make atonement.'

notes.meaning: These verses summarize all the instructions given in chapters 13 and 14 for various skin diseases, head sores, mildew in fabrics, and mold in houses. They bring together every rule regarding bodily swellings, rashes, and bright spots. God provided a clear, complete guide to help Israel detect rot wherever it showed up.

The purpose of these laws was to guide the priests so they could teach the people what was clean and what was unclean. The priests did not invent their own standards, but followed God's clear rules. These commands helped the entire community stay holy and fit to live in the presence of God.
